taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from MI6.1-3 | Central Nervous System Infections.

words.clue: Inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, commonly caused by bacterial or viral infection.
The most common route of bacterial spread to the CNS, occurring via bacteremia from respiratory tract colonization.
Appearance of cerebrospinal fluid when bacterial meningitis is present, with cell counts exceeding 200 cells per mm³.
Yellow discoloration of cerebrospinal fluid indicating subarachnoid hemorrhage or chronic infection such as tuberculous meningitis.
Increased number of white blood cells in the cerebrospinal fluid observed in both bacterial and viral meningitis.
Form of chronic meningitis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the commonest cause of chronic meningitis in India.
Encapsulated fungal organism causing meningitis in immunocompromised patients, detectable by India ink preparation.
Free-living parasitic amoeba that causes rapidly fatal primary amoebic meningoencephalitis acquired from warm freshwater.
Type of cellular predominance in cerebrospinal fluid during viral meningitis and tuberculous meningitis.
Type of parasitic meningitis caused by Naegleria fowleri transmitted through swimming in warm freshwater.
System of serum proteins that mediates bacterial killing and is a primary host defense against encapsulated organisms.
Primary host defense mechanism whereby complement-mediated coating of bacteria enhances their destruction by phagocytes.
